verdict.tagline: Grand strategy plagued by technical instability and broken warfare.
for_you_if: you enjoy untangling deeply complex economic systems
you can master steep learning curves
not_for_you_if: you encounter launcher errors and startup crashes
you rely on functional naval invasion mechanics
you want smooth performance on lower end hardware

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Players face immediate startup crashes, unhelpful tutorials, and launcher errors.

claims.claim: The game fails to launch or crashes during startup and initialization.

citations.review_text: Disappointed because I was really excited to play this game, but it wouldn't launch. I had to uninstall and reinstall it to get it to launch the first time and thought "okay, this is fine now." Come around the next day to actually sink some time into it and the same problem of it sits on "initialising game" and then won't respond. Looks like it's a well known issue especially in the past couple of years so don't waste your time or your money on this one :(

Junk, I installed it at first on my game drive, it wouldn't launch and said it couldn't find the files.  k, fine, uninstalled and reinstalled on the C drive and it opens but crashes on the launch page.  not great.  I'll uninstall and reinstall one more time and see if I can get a refund.
Can't even open the game. Errors pop up, freezes during initiation after the launcher. Way to offer a free play week only for there to still be massive bugs.

I´ve tried to try this game. Installed it, lauched it, crashed. Tried again, crashed again, then uninstalled. This is the first time in about 30 years of gaming that this happens to me. Steam should not allow games in this state to be on its store.
Why the game is Crashing in the launching page?
Stuck on initializing game.  Game never gets past the splash screen.

claims.claim: The in-game tutorials are described as useless and confusing, explaining almost nothing about how to actually play the game.

citations.review_text: I have no idea wtf is going on. The tutorials are basically useless in the grand scheme of things. If I have to use hour upon hour of youtube videos to understand a game then it fails to be fun.

Such a confusing game. I went through the tutorial and the game explains almost nothing to you. They just throw you without any useful explanation to how to play this game.

looks fun when you understand it but very difficult to get into it.

This game is way too complicated for beginners. I tried watching a 20-minute YouTube tutorial, but when I played, the UI was different, so I could not find anything. The in-game tutorial feels useless: things happen, but you do not really understand how or why. The UI is overwhelming, and the 2-hour demo ended before I could really get into it. So I think that is where it ends for me. The videos look nice and really made me want to play, though!

paradox launcher, cant limit fps

citations.review_text: Worst DLC pricing in the entire industry, and they're not even worth it on a sale. The game is worth like $20-30 max with all DLCs because it's not even particularly deep or advanced, it's just hard to learn all the menus initially.

Not worth it. confusing, graphics may look good, but the content is still lacking, its another HOI4, CK3, EU4, ect but for 1800s, you need about 50 thousand overpriced stupid DLCS to have even a smidge of fun.
feck off Paradox with your overpriced bs.

I would strongly recommend Victoria 2, and buying Hearts of Darkness maybe if you want more options and modding capabilities.

Game requires internet to start first time to download VS dependancies from Microsoft website to install Paradox Launcher, without internet the download fails and game does not start.

Initially, I couldn't get the game to load. Then my dumb ass figured out that in addition to the game's almost 18GB file size, it [b] requires [/b] an extra [b] 10GB [/b] of available space to compile shaders or some sh*t like that.

claims.claim: Reviewers note performance issues and crashing when running the game on laptops or lower-end hardware.

citations.review_text: It's a great game. Steep learning curve, but worth it. I find a lot of satisfaction in liberalising my country and beating the hell out of others. I also like to imagine how the history I'm doing is formed, and imagining a history class teaching why brazil owns half of South America. Of course, it does take a bit of a PC to run it, my laptop couldn't run this at all, but once I switched to a desktop I can play it really smoothly. If you like paradox and these type of games, I'd say buy it. And unlike Hoi4, playing with 0 DLCs is great anyways.
i like the game but dont try running on a laptop im traying and it doesnt like it

I'm gonna be real wait at least like another year before even thinking about investing your time, money and expectations for this game. Even after all these years it still somehow feels like it needs a few more years in the oven and somewhat bare-bones: warfare is nausea inducingly bad, optimization is horrible (even though I have a low-end pc, I still see the obvious performance issues even in high-end pc's), it needs at least ten patches on top of each other to fix all the bugs, AI is braindead on both ends of the spectrum which is genuinely awe-inspiring (not accepting even white peace when they're %60 occupied, throwing bodies at my front until they have more than a million dead and etc.) Overall, wait unless you just want to play to mess around, it's sadly not worth it.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience game crashes later in campaigns, specifically in the twentieth century or on specific calendar dates such as August 5th.

citations.review_text: was having a lot of fun playing this game however my game is unplayable after 1910 -- frequently crashing every few days of in game time, which is unfortunate because I can't see the culmination of my playthrough. I think it's from memory leaks

Cannot recommend in current state. Had two major bugs in the same short run. First, enemy's armies were literally doubled. Even when you click on them for more information, showed them twice. Had to full restart game and it fixed itself. However, later in that same run, the game just crashes August 5. I can't do anything about it, tried taking different actions, etc. Just hard crashes every time on August 5th. A buggy mess. I regret having had to spend so much money just for something that doesn't even work. Some very good ideas here, but I am essentially paying 80 dollars to be a bug-tester for Paradox...
Game keeps crashing on a specific date, so my long save is now unplayable.

What can I say? Scandinavian charlatans baited me into buying several expansions after I played it at launch (I've played about 150 hours in total).

Yes, the game has improved.

Has it gained soul? Still not. 
Are the naval invasion bugs fixed? Still not. 
Has the game stopped crashing in the 20th century? Still not. 
etc.

The game isn't worth the money, even though it has ambitions on the scale of the British Empire.

citations.review_text:
What can I say? Scandinavian charlatans baited me into buying several expansions after I played it at launch (I've played about 150 hours in total).

Yes, the game has improved.

Has it gained soul? Still not. 
Are the naval invasion bugs fixed? Still not.

etc.

The game isn't worth the money, even though it has ambitions on the scale of the British Empire.

I'm loving this game and think that the things it aims to accomplish (economy and politics) are done extremely well - the polulation and manufacturing systems are fantastic and very satisfying to play around. I've also found the UI to be very nice (it has its problems in terms of layout but the way its built where you can keep going deeper and deeper into any menu by hovering over various pieces of text is great).

But I can't in good conscience recommend this game to anyone who has ambitions of conquest as its so buggy and frustrating.

If you focus only on the economy of the game then it is a great game, and you can still conquer fairly easily and without much trouble as long as you stick to only doing small scale land-only wars. In those aspects I'm loving this game and do intend to continue playing it.

But anything involving navies is terrible and sucks all the fun out of the game for a while. Theres a bug where your navy gets stuck on a sea tile unable to do anything, move, or get transfered or anything, the game says that it see's the navy as being in a battle and so it can't perform any other actions - the only 'solution' is to disband (destroy) it and then rebuild it from scratch, that can mean that you need to spend 10 years rebuilding your main fleet depending on your circumstances, and the game only lasts 100 years! This glich apparently can happen after a land invasion (which is a very common scenario in large scale wars) and theres a slew of other similar but slightly less bad gliches.

several navies on the same time being unable to merge but if you transfer all the ships between them 1 by 1 then that works; 2 armies on the same tile sometimes being 'unable to reach each other'; enemy armies sometimes being able to walk onto your land without there being a front available and so you cant fight them; etc etc

Frankly all of these are unacceptable in a finished game (It is still being developed and probably will continue to be for at least 5 m…

claims.claim: Reviewers point out a lack of historical flavor, unique events, and distinct national focus trees compared to other grand strategy titles.

citations.review_text: Really would have liked to see more historical events or even just...interesting events in general for flavour. Warfare and politics in the game are rather bland. 7/10 imo. It's ok, get it on discount.

The RNG kills the game for me. Basically nothing historical happens. Every sandbox you play is just silly and whacky. If it was just alittle more structured like HOI4 I'd enjoy it more. Almost no historical events, the AI can't handle civil strife and just opts for constant civil wars instead of painfully easy reforms. I could have gotten a thousand hours out of this easy were it not for the poor RNG. now every time I think about playing it, I know things are just gonna get whacky and wierd and just not fun for me.

I'm a big Paradox fan but this game is disappointingly bland. Once you learn how to play there's no depth to it. Every nation is basically the same, in game events are few and far between, and combat has little character with no unique units or tactics. 

Compare this to something like HOI where each nation gets its own focus tree, unique units, and a plethora of unique events. 

This game has the bones to be great but it's underdeveloped. Recommend waiting 5 years until they release 5-10 expansions that should be part of the base game.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as having a steep learning curve and being difficult to understand or master for beginners.

citations.review_text: It's a great game. Steep learning curve, but worth it. I find a lot of satisfaction in liberalising my country and beating the hell out of others. I also like to imagine how the history I'm doing is formed, and imagining a history class teaching why brazil owns half of South America. Of course, it does take a bit of a PC to run it, my laptop couldn't run this at all, but once I switched to a desktop I can play it really smoothly. If you like paradox and these type of games, I'd say buy it. And unlike Hoi4, playing with 0 DLCs is great anyways.

This, as all grand strategy games from paradox, isn't for everyone. Steep learning curve, lack of defined goal, information overload, lack of QoL.
But among the grand strategy games this is my favorite by far. A wonderful exploration of an important time in history.

A very enjoyable industrialization/proletarization-focused strategy game. As with other Paradox games, it is quite difficult to learn and master, but very rewarding once its mechanics start to click (especially if you enjoy fantasizing about council republics overthrowing monarchs and oligarchs. Ha).
Very steep learning curve but lots of resources to help - incredibly deep economy sim!

claims.claim: Updates introduce bugs and stability issues, including crashes during campaigns, diplomatic plays, or when running on specific APIs like Vulkan.

citations.review_text: I love this game, have loved it for quite a long time. Now it is completely unplayable, creating a campaign has like a 1 in 3 chance of crashing before reaching the mid game. I will not recommend for anyone to buy it in the current state.

After update 1.13.10, this literally broke the game. on vulkan? immediate crash, exit code 1. use DX11? good luck running the game at anything more than 1fps. and you crash when you reach february 1836. With this situation, it is 100% unplayable.

In 1.13.10 when you transfer a state in a diplomatic play the game crashes immediately, which makes the game completely unplayable (at least for me). 

You don't have to release the game if you don't know whether it's playable okay? It's frustrating how Paradox is ruining this game when it's getting better.

claims.claim: Multiplayer sessions suffer from out-of-sync errors, netcode problems, and save corruption over time.

citations.review_text:
I think Victoria 3 is a good game. It has an engaging gameplay loop, fun diplomacy, interesting politics, and several other positives I cannot be bothered to name right now. Because, this game is tarnished by one major thing. You see, I have friends, surprisingly, and I like to play this game with those friends. But because Paradox can't seem to be bothered to fix out-of-sync issues and netcode, I feel compelled to leave a negative review as a sign of protest and dissatisfaction. 

(And the issues are [i] really [/i] bad, we could barely make it 3 years to a week in game without having to restart the lobby, it's frustrating and made us all sad. For we love this game, we do. So let me play this game with my friends? (Jk, I know Paradox won't read this lol, lmao.))

I love Victoria but multiplayer on the current version is unplayable. After 20 - 30 years in game the entire save corrupts from military/character mismatches. Meaning you have to simply enjoy the game until the 1870s which should be mid-game but instead that is your end since the entire save with your friends will crash out. Singleplayer this has no issue, its playable and enjoyable. But if you want to play with friends in the current state you have to roll back to before 1.13.x in order to have a stable game.
Please fix desync issues, it's a bit silly. 1895 with two players, and the game is basically unplayable.

Please do not buy this game - at least not in its current state. It is extremely unoptimized and suffers from constant lag spikes, crashes, and out-of-sync errors in multiplayer.

Looking at their track record with other games, this isn't an isolated issue. Paradox only cares about pumping out new DLCs instead of fixing core bugs. This game has been out for over three years, and they still haven't done anything to clean up this mess.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that creating a campaign crashes before reaching the mid-game, that updating to version 1.13.10 causes immediate crashes on Vulkan and frame rate drops on DX11, and that transferring a state in a diplomatic play causes the game to crash immediately.

citations.review_text: I love this game, have loved it for quite a long time. Now it is completely unplayable, creating a campaign has like a 1 in 3 chance of crashing before reaching the mid game. I will not recommend for anyone to buy it in the current state.

After update 1.13.10, this literally broke the game. on vulkan? immediate crash, exit code 1. use DX11? good luck running the game at anything more than 1fps. and you crash when you reach february 1836. With this situation, it is 100% unplayable.

In 1.13.10 when you transfer a state in a diplomatic play the game crashes immediately, which makes the game completely unplayable (at least for me). 

You don't have to release the game if you don't know whether it's playable okay? It's frustrating how Paradox is ruining this game when it's getting better.

claims.claim: The military and war system features broken frontline mechanics, unexpected army movement routing, and problematic naval transport and invasion supply limits.

citations.review_text:
I wanted to love this game, but after hundreds of hours, the military system is actively punishing players for its own nonsensical logic.

1. The Broken Frontline System: Armies teleport across impassable borders, random frontlines split out of nowhere, and tiny enemy enclaves instantly become the "main front," forcing your main army on home soil to sit around doing nothing while taking supply penalties.

2. Forced Surrender ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥: The game will force you into an unconditional surrender just because an AI snuck a tiny unit onto a worthless tile for a few months, completely ignoring your actual economic and military strength.

3. The New Naval DLC Disaster: Thanks to the new naval mechanics, the mighty British Empire in 1836 can somehow only transport like two handfuls of battalions across the ocean. Because the same ignorant developers who ignore the terrible war system decided that a ship can only carry 0,7 battalions

Could be a great game, and I keep coming to it again and again, but sooner or later I end up in a war and I remember why I rage quit the last game. THE F***ING, 100% disfunctional and completely bugged army movement!

Until Paradox fixes this I call this game completely unplayable

The game was very good, and is probably one of the better paradox games.

That being said, in the current update the game is essentially completely broken with wars. Armies will take routes across the entire globe by sea to attack a front that shares a land border with you. Troops will attack in all directions, then the enemy will have a civil war and because thats not your war you no longer control that area, so your supply lines are instantly cut.

Game was better at release solely because the war system is such a joke, trying to push through hudson bay to columbia district? youre gonna need ships to walk across the canadian wilderness! took over guatemala through a naval invasion and now trying to get your troops home? screw you! the HQ is in the pacific so sail around south america to get them back. Atleast when the economy was bad I wasnt dealing with this bs

not for me, really just couldn't get into it or really understand it. its first and foremost an economic simulator of the 1800's which i think could be really fun and im sure anyone would have a blast playing it but i just couldn't really understand it and for that reason im out.
-Barbara
Great game. One of the best economic Simulators. It also have a good war system. I will take a bit until you understand it and master it but it is very fun.

claims.claim: DLC pricing is considered exorbitant and overpriced relative to the content provided.

citations.review_text: Avoid all Paradox games at all costs. A once proud and amazing studio is gone, and in its place are broken games, and endless over priced DLC products that only change the game incrementally. They update policy gives you a third of new DLC's, but without any way of actually manipulating the new mechanics unless you pay for the whole thing. You might say, 'then don't download the updates', to which I will point out that all bug fixes are handled in these updates, and updates are tied to mods, so if you don't update the game nothing gets fixed and the mods break. Either way, you update the game and the publisher makes the game worse, you don't update and the game slowly loses functionality, your choice.

Honestly I have really tried with this game but I can honestly say having played most Paradox titles and a host of other strategy and worldbuilders that this is the most unenjoyable and annoying game I have ever played. The RNG is insanely biased, the AI works as a wolfpack and makes sure you end up rage quitting and coming back like an addict trying to get some return on your investment, because by the end of the game's dev cycle which includes them dropping fixes that should be free for 30 euros, you have spent twice as much as you would for the best games on the market in any category. 

Need to pass a law to avoid civil war? It will take 5 years even if 80% of the country supports it. Prepare a war and invade with 2-1 superiority? You watch as your commanders suddenly lose the ability to fight and seem to always lose the one decisive battle which means the war goes on for another 2 years. Try to colonise? the AI cuts directly in front and has absurd buffs.

And the economy mechanic is even more laughable. I have seen AI countries with massive armies, economies and seemingly endless spending and bad laws and yet they never run a debt. Until I play them and they immediately become Greece on steroids. Prussia into Germany always means not doing any construction for basically 50 years. France is being in debt no matter what you do and then getting curbstomped by AI Germany that had no problems. Countries with no GDP can spend as much as they like which is hilarious given the game ties your credit limit to your buildings and you collect 0 dividend taxes without progressive laws (which AI never do). And wars with huge casualties do not make a dent in their economies. 

Russia is the only country worth playing. It's stupidly easy and gets boring by like 1900 but its hilarious that the "dynamic" politics system allows Russia to have high literacy, a massive working class, no SoL and yet there is no revolution. But try passing a different trade law as Germany and w…

I would like the game, if it was playable for a reasaonble price. But the DLC costs are extortiate. To go from the base game, to selectively having the 'good bits' it'd be over $50. While it's on sale. And I could eat that, but it feels bad doing that, when I know in another year I'll be in the same situation.

And that would be fine, except that if you don't have the DLC, the game is designed to remind you of that, it's obnoxious. We get it paradox, we look like walking wallets.

This game was great until they changed the naval mechanics to whatever this is. There are now too many undisclosed mechanics/bugs that the game is essentially unplayable. I  bought the season pass for this but this was probably a massive mistake considering how terrible the state of the game has been since the naval update. There are a few areas which improved massively, treaties, straits and general diplomacy but when you combine that with broken naval transports any island  playstyle (excluding the UK) is too spastic to bother with.  Then there's the changes to conscripts which are good until you're mid war and can't combine it with any other army abroad (unless it also has conscripts) because it'll delete them all. Now the game doesn't say it'll do this you just get to lose the war instead as punishment for not knowing ahead of time.

There are also so many features/mechanics that its near impossible to actually exploit them properly because the game's length is too short to use them. Its like jamming EU4s mechanics into a game that lasts for a tenth of the time. Then also with every update theres more events which just add a level of tedium clicking through them all, its the same problem that CK and stellaris have where there are so many events included in the DLC that you can't properly play the game without having to either spam through them or slow your game right down that it takes a few days to get through a game. I genuinely believe this is a design problem these games have where the expectation is to play slow and properly consider your actions but everything takes so long to do you have to shift to 5 speed to actually get anywhere. I love this game! i played more than 1300 hours. However, most recent DLC changed the game a lot! managing overseas troop transfer became extremely difficult. For example, I am playing as Japan, I have 100 troops I need to transfer. I have a fleet with 120 unit carrying capacity, I start an invasion to overseas region, my army split and only 20 of them are taken onboard! I have absolutely no idea why! tehre are other issues around naval controls! They just messed up sooooo much I could not recommend anyone this game at this point!!!

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game lacks content variety for major nations like the USA and Germany compared to other regions.

citations.review_text: It is quite fun although it is lacking in some regards when it comes to making things personal. One of the best parts of Paradox games like CK3 or HOI4 is making the country you play your own and the unique differences but in this its just different cultures and religions buying more or less of maybe one product and a handful of journal entries for a couple of the countries. They're adding more with DLC but it's missing a bit at the moment. Still good.

It’s been almost 4 years and there still is no additional content for the USA, Germany, great wars, USA civil war, Great Depression, or scramble for Africa. Central Asia has more unique events than the USA or Germany… these devs are so out of touch with the community
